description: Set what the person is at an event for, and whether other attendees there may find them. Use it for "set my intent", "I am here to buy", "tell people I am looking for investors", "make me findable". ASK TWO QUESTIONS AND PASS BOTH ANSWERS IN THEIR OWN WORDS: "What are you here for?" is `headline`, and "Who do you want to meet?" is `lookingFor`. THOSE TWO SENTENCES ARE THE BADGE. Together with their name they are the whole of what makes a person findable at this event, and they are what the matcher reads to decide who they are shown to, so ask both, pass both, and do not compress them, tidy them or invent them. `intent` is OPTIONAL and is a quick pick rather than a question you owe: pass one of Buyer, Vendor, Networker or Social only when the person actually said one of those words, and otherwise leave it out, because the server works the category out from what they wrote and falls back to Networker exactly as their badge in the app does. IF THEY NAME A CATEGORY OF THEIR OWN - "investor", "director", anything - pass it as `label` and it is kept as their word rather than refused; never talk them out of it and never map it onto one of the four yourself. `discoverable` is a SEPARATE and REQUIRED answer and is never inferred from the intent: ask the person, because true puts them in the list other attendees can see and false keeps them out of it. TWO CALLS, ALWAYS: call it first with no `confirm` to get back a sentence saying exactly what will change plus a `confirmToken`, show that sentence to the person, then call it again with confirm true and that token. The token lasts two minutes, works once, and stops working if any argument changes. It requires a personal connector token: a shared one can read but cannot change anything. It changes that one person's badge at one event and reaches nobody else's. A badge with one of the two sentences still blank cannot be found by anybody yet, so it is refused naming the sentence that is missing rather than written. CLOUD 181a: `firstName` IS THE THIRD THING THE BADGE IS MADE OF, beside the two sentences above, and it is OPTIONAL in the same way they are. Pass it when the person has just told you their name or asked to change it and leave it out every other time: an omitted name leaves theirs alone and an invented one would rename them. Until this unit there was no door onto that field outside the app, which is why a person who had only ever used an assistant or a browser could not finish a badge however many sentences they wrote. A name the badge cannot take refuses the whole call rather than writing half of it, and the refusal says which thing was wrong with it.

confirm.description: Leave this out on the first call. Pass true with confirmToken to commit.

confirmToken.description: The token the preview returned. Required when confirm is true.

discoverable.description: REQUIRED, and never inferred from the intent: true puts them in the list other attendees at that event can see, false keeps them out of it. Ask the person which they want; a missing or non-boolean answer is refused rather than defaulted.

eventId.description: OPTIONAL. Omit for the event the person is currently in, which is the usual case. Only pass one if they named a different show, and it must be one they have already joined.

firstName.description: OPTIONAL. The person's FIRST NAME, 2 to 40 characters of letters, spaces, hyphens and apostrophes. It is the THIRD thing a badge is made of, beside the two sentences: a badge with no name cannot be found by other attendees either. Pass it only when they have just told you their name or asked to change it; leaving it out keeps whatever their badge already says and never clears it. Never invent a name, never shorten one they gave you, and never pass a surname.

headline.description: What they are here for, in their OWN words, up to 280 characters. This is the first of the two sentences the badge is made of, so ask "What are you here for?" and pass what they say. FULL SENTENCES ARE THE POINT: it is read by the matcher that decides who they are shown to and it is what strangers read about them, so "raising a seed round for a logistics startup" beats "raising money". Phone numbers, email addresses and links are removed on the server, because other attendees read it. Leaving it out keeps whatever their badge already says and never clears it.

intent.description: OPTIONAL quick pick, not a question you have to ask. One of Buyer, Vendor, Networker or Social, as the person said it; case and surrounding spaces do not matter. Leave it out when they did not name one of those four words: the server derives the category from the two sentences and falls back to Networker, which is what their badge in the app does. A word outside the four does NOT go here - it goes in `label`, where it is kept rather than refused.

intentText.description: OPTIONAL, and the OLDER NAME for `lookingFor`: it writes the same badge line. Prefer `lookingFor`, which is the badge's own word for it, and pass only one of the two. What they are looking for, in their OWN words, up to 280 characters. FULL SENTENCES ARE WELCOME and are what this field is for: it is read by the matcher that decides who they are shown, so "raising a seed round for a logistics startup, and looking for operators who have scaled a warehouse" matches better than "raising money". Do not compress what they said to save room. Phone numbers, email addresses and links are removed from it on the server, because other attendees read it. Leave it out to keep whatever their badge already says; sending an empty string also leaves it alone.

label.description: OPTIONAL. Their own word for what they are, when none of the four fits: "Investor", "Director", "Press". Up to 24 characters, letters, spaces and hyphens only. It is KEPT AND SHOWN as their word and is never refused for being outside the four; the server still files one of the four behind it so the match list can say why two people fit. Pass it only when the person named it themselves - it is a fact about them, so never invent one and never tidy theirs.

lookingFor.description: Who they want to meet, in their OWN words, up to 280 characters. This is the second of the two sentences the badge is made of, so ask "Who do you want to meet?" and pass what they say. It is the SAME badge line the older `intentText` argument writes, under the badge's own name for it; pass one or the other, not both. Phone numbers, email addresses and links are removed on the server. Leaving it out keeps whatever their badge already says and never clears it.

requestId.description: Your own id for this change, at least 8 characters. Sending the same one twice with the same arguments returns the first result instead of writing again.
